	<item>
		<title>Lifelike Birds Emerge from Foliage in Painted Paper Reliefs by The Paper Ark</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/the-paper-ark-birds-relief-nature-watercolors/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Kate Mothes]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Thu, 30 Jul 2026 17:48:19 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Nature]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[birds]]></category>

		<category><![CDATA[paper]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[relief]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[The Paper Ark]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=476301</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/paper-ark-2.jpg" alt="Lifelike Birds Emerge from Foliage in Painted Paper Reliefs by The Paper Ark" />The duo aims to raise awareness of biodiversity and conservation by evoking a sense of wonder similar to what we feel in nature.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. ]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/paper-ark-2.jpg" alt="Lifelike Birds Emerge from Foliage in Painted Paper Reliefs by The Paper Ark" />


<p>From meticulously cut and painted pieces of paper, realistic birds emerge amid foliage and forests in compositions by <a href="https://www.thepaperark.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">The Paper Ark</a>. The collaborative practice of Nayan Shrimali and Venus Bird, which focuses on intricate <a href="/tags/the-paper-ark">paper reliefs</a>, also centers on ecology by illustrating real species and their habitats around the world. The duo aims to raise awareness of biodiversity and conservation by evoking a sense of wonder akin to how we also often feel in nature.</p>



<p>The artists recently exhibited a number of the pieces shown here with Antler Gallery at Seattle Art Fair, and &#8220;Great Green Macaws&#8221; appeared in the <a href="https://www.audubon.org/magazine/issues/spring-2026" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Spring 2026 issue</a> of <em>Audubon Magazine</em>. See more on The Paper Ark&#8217;s <a href="https://www.instagram.com/thepaperark/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2500" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/paper-ark-8.jpg" alt="a painted paper composition of two realistic hyacinth macaws sitting amid foliage" class="wp-image-476308" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/paper-ark-8.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/paper-ark-8-640x800.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/paper-ark-8-960x1200.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/paper-ark-8-768x960.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/paper-ark-8-1229x1536.jpg 1229w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/paper-ark-8-1638x2048.jpg 1638w" sizes="(max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Hyacinth Macaw&#8221;</figcaption></figure>

		<item>
		<title>Zac Henderson Venerates Devil&#8217;s Tower in Bold Black-and-White Photos</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/zac-henderson-devils-tower-photographs/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Kate Mothes]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Thu, 30 Jul 2026 17:10:06 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Nature]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Photography]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[black and white]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[geology]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[landscapes]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Wyoming]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Zac Henderson]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=476286</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/henderson-6.jpg" alt="Zac Henderson Venerates Devil&#8217;s Tower in Bold Black-and-White Photos" />Henderson also captures the changing light and the otherworldly textures and ochres of the iconic rock.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/zac-henderson-devils-tower-photographs/">Zac Henderson Venerates Devil&#8217;s Tower in Bold Black-and-White Photos</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/henderson-6.jpg" alt="Zac Henderson Venerates Devil&#8217;s Tower in Bold Black-and-White Photos" />


<p>In 1906, Devil&#8217;s Tower in northeastern Wyoming became the first national monument in the U.S., preserving a little more than <a href="https://www.npca.org/case-studies/devil-s-tower-national-monument" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">1,300 acres</a> around the 867-foot-tall column of igneous rock. Amid the rolling hills of the plains, it can be seen from miles around, and it&#8217;s been a sacred site and gathering place for myriad Indigenous American tribes, who refer to it by names like Bear Lodge or Bear&#8217;s House.</p>



<p>One <a href="https://www.visitrapidcity.com/blog/post/the-story-of-devils-tower-national-monument/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">oral narrative</a> describes how bears attacked a group of seven girls, and the ground swelled up to push the children toward the sky. There, they became the constellation Pleiades, or the &#8220;<a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleiades" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Seven Sisters</a>,&#8221; which can be seen over the monument. In other stories, the distinctive striations around the landform are said to have been created by bears clawing at the earth to try to reach the girls.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2500" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/henderson-5.jpg" alt="a black-and-white photograph of Devil's Tower with a cloud's shadow darkening the base" class="wp-image-476296" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/henderson-5.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/henderson-5-640x800.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/henderson-5-960x1200.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/henderson-5-768x960.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/henderson-5-1229x1536.jpg 1229w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/henderson-5-1638x2048.jpg 1638w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<p>For nomadic photographer <a href="https://www.zachenderson.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Zac Henderson</a>, the unique geological formation proved an irresistible subject. He travels the continent making <a href="/tags/zac-henderson">dreamy images</a> of landscapes and natural phenomena, often merging reality with a sense of the uncanny. When it comes to geology, there&#8217;s hardly a more iconic example than Devil&#8217;s Tower, which formed tens of millions of years ago as a column of hardened magma was gradually revealed through erosion.</p>



<p>Henderson captures the moodiness of clouds casting shadows in black-and-white images that are redolent of Ansel Adams&#8217; deep tonal shifts. Even though the monument sees hundreds of thousands of visitors every year, there is a sense of isolation and unadulterated wonder, as if we are encountering it for the first time. Henderson also captures the changing light and otherworldly textures and ochres of the rock face, which can be seen from a network of paths around its one-mile base circumference.</p>



<p>See more timelapses on Henderson&#8217;s <a href="https://vimeo.com/zndrson" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Vimeo</a>, and explore more on <a href="https://www.behance.net/zachenderson" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Behance</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2500" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/henderson-7.jpg" alt="a photograph of the texture of stone on Devil's Tower in Wyoming" class="wp-image-476298" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/henderson-7.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/henderson-7-640x800.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/henderson-7-960x1200.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/henderson-7-768x960.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/henderson-7-1229x1536.jpg 1229w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/henderson-7-1638x2048.jpg 1638w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2500" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/henderson-2.jpg" alt="a black-and-white photograph of Devil's Tower" class="wp-image-476294" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/henderson-2.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/henderson-2-640x800.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/henderson-2-960x1200.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/henderson-2-768x960.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/henderson-2-1229x1536.jpg 1229w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/henderson-2-1638x2048.jpg 1638w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="800" height="450" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/henderson.gif" alt="a gif of a timelapse of weather moving over Devil's Tower in Wyoming" class="wp-image-476300"/></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2500" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/henderson-3.jpg" alt="a black-and-white photograph of Devil's Tower with a cloud's shadow darkening the base" class="wp-image-476295" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/henderson-3.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/henderson-3-640x800.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/henderson-3-960x1200.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/henderson-3-768x960.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/henderson-3-1229x1536.jpg 1229w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/henderson-3-1638x2048.jpg 1638w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>

			</item>
		<item>
		<title>Janice Yang&#8217;s Symbol-Rich Paintings Conjure Dreams and the Desire for Home</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/janice-yang-kitchens-home-salmon-paintings/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Kate Mothes]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Thu, 30 Jul 2026 14:40:26 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[cooking]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[family]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[fish]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[home]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[immigration]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Janice Yang]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[painting]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[South Korea]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=476275</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-4.jpg" alt="Janice Yang&#8217;s Symbol-Rich Paintings Conjure Dreams and the Desire for Home" />Years of labor and adaptation as a first-generation immigrant shaped the artist's approach to painting.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/janice-yang-kitchens-home-salmon-paintings/">Janice Yang&#8217;s Symbol-Rich Paintings Conjure Dreams and the Desire for Home</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-4.jpg" alt="Janice Yang&#8217;s Symbol-Rich Paintings Conjure Dreams and the Desire for Home" />


<p>At the age of 14, <a href="https://janiceyangart.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Janice Yang</a> and her family emigrated from South Korea to the U.S. in the wake of a financial crisis that upended their sense of security. (Incidentally, the Korean stock market is experiencing a historic crash this month in the wake of <a href="https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/south-korea-stock-market-crash-092957385.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">unwinding global trade</a> in the AI sector.) Displaced from everything they knew, her family had to start again. &#8220;Our stable economic situation in Korea changed to more precarious working-class reality in the U.S., where repeated business failures left us in a lot of debt,&#8221; Yang tells Colossal.</p>



<p>For two decades, Yang worked unpaid at her family&#8217;s small sushi restaurant, where she dreamed of eventually pursuing her studies to become an artist, all while navigating a new culture and helping to carry her family&#8217;s financial burden. &#8220;These years of labor and adaptation have profoundly shaped my identity as a first-generation immigrant and my artistic practice,&#8221; she says. Her figurative paintings, which often center self-portraits amid busy kitchens, are accompanied by dream-like clouds and distant vistas that open up in walls and windows or float around the figures&#8217; heads. There&#8217;s also a lot of fish.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1598" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-8.jpg" alt="a painting of two women in a kitchen centered around a skillet that has a huge flame in it" class="wp-image-476283" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-8.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-8-640x511.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-8-960x767.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-8-768x614.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-8-1536x1227.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;The Hours Between (노을의 색들)&#8221; (2026), salmon ash and oil on canvas, 48 x 60 inches</figcaption></figure>



<p>Whether filleted, whole, chopped, or cooking, salmon are prevalent in many of Yang&#8217;s compositions. In a sense, they were the artist&#8217;s constant companions for years. &#8220;Every day, I saw salmon getting flayed and prepped in plastic wrap to be stored into the fridge,&#8221; she says. &#8220;I would develop personal feelings to salmon and personify them, since they reminded me the unfulfilled dream I had as an artist.&#8221; They also represent the desire to return home.</p>



<p>Every year, salmon complete the physically demanding biological process of spawning, in which they migrate from the ocean to their native freshwater streams and rivers to lay eggs. Huge numbers of the fish home in on the place they were born, fighting their way upstream to ensure the survival of the next generation. &#8220;This related to my feelings and hopes to reach my dream and find the sense of belonging in a new place where I felt often lost,&#8221; Yang says. Occasionally, her paintings incorporate salmon ash along with acrylic and oil pigments.</p>



<p>The artist also nods to symbolic elements of Korean art history and visual culture, such as a scroll painting by <a href="https://smarthistory.org/artist/an-gyeon/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Ahn Gyeon</a>, a court painter during Joseon Dynasty in the 15th century. The unfurled work sits on the lap of the figure in &#8220;Ahn Gyeon’s Dream Journey to the Peach Blossom Land.&#8221; The painting is now held in a collection in Japan, and Yang describes how Koreans hope to see the painting returned to its homeland someday. Korean aesthetics converge with classical Western artistic methods like one-point perspective. Yang says, &#8220;For me, this blending of visual languages becomes a way to think through ideas of home, coexistence, and contradiction, and to reflect on the complexity of diasporic identity.&#8221;</p>



<p>Starting next month, Yang will be an artist-in-residence at <a href="https://www.gallerymomo.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Gallery MOMO</a> in Johannesburg, South Africa, where she will also present an exhibition. And in September, she will commence a nine-month artist residency at <a href="https://lillstreet.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Lillstreet Art Center</a> in Chicago, where she will teach, in addition to being a visiting lecturer at the School of the Art Institute&#8217;s Painting and Drawing Department. See more on Yang&#8217;s <a href="https://www.instagram.com/janiceyangart/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2592" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-3.jpg" alt="a painting of a young Asian woman on her hands and knees in a kitchen, holding a large salmon near the floor as water spills from a sink above" class="wp-image-476278" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-3.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-3-640x829.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-3-960x1244.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-3-768x995.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-3-1185x1536.jpg 1185w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-3-1580x2048.jpg 1580w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Chaekgado (책가도)&#8221; (2026), oil on canvas, 36 x 48 inches</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1326" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-5.jpg" alt="a painting of two women preparing salmon in a kitchen" class="wp-image-476280" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-5.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-5-640x424.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-5-960x636.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-5-768x509.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-5-1536x1018.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;From the Cracks (틈의 소리)&#8221; (2026), salmon ash and oil on canvas, 72 x 48 inches</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2726" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-6.jpg" alt="a painting of a young Asian woman cleaning a salmon in a kitchen" class="wp-image-476281" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-6.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-6-640x872.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-6-960x1308.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-6-768x1047.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-6-1127x1536.jpg 1127w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-6-1503x2048.jpg 1503w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Kata/카타 (カタ)&#8221; (2026), salmon ash and oil on canvas, 40 x 52 inches</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2322" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-7.jpg" alt="a hexagonal painting of a young Asian woman cleaning a salmon in a kitchen" class="wp-image-476282" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-7.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-7-640x743.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-7-960x1115.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-7-768x892.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-7-1323x1536.jpg 1323w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-7-1764x2048.jpg 1764w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">“Inside Out” (2026), oil on panel, 12 x 12 inches</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2664" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-9.jpg" alt="a painting of a young woman seated on the floor of a kitchen surrounded by filleted salmon" class="wp-image-476284" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-9.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-9-640x852.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-9-960x1279.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-9-768x1023.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-9-1153x1536.jpg 1153w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-9-1538x2048.jpg 1538w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Threshold&#8221; (2023), oil on canvas, 30 x 40 inches</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1511" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-2.jpg" alt="a painting of a young woman seated at an easel near a kitchen with a flame under a skillet" class="wp-image-476277" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-2.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-2-640x484.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-2-960x725.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-2-768x580.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-2-1536x1160.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Bento (弁当)&#8221; (2026), acrylic and oil on panel, 12 x 16 inches</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1181" height="1657" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-1.jpg" alt="a painting of a young Asian woman standing, lost in thought, amid abstract areas of color" class="wp-image-476276" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-1.jpg 1181w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-1-640x898.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-1-960x1347.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-1-768x1078.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/yang-1-1095x1536.jpg 1095w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1181px) 100vw, 1181px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Between&#8221; (2025), Hanji collage, oil on canvas, 35 x 25 inches</figcaption></figure>

										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/hottea-3.jpg" alt="August 2026 Opportunities: Open Calls, Residencies, and Grants for Artists" />


<p>Every month, we share opportunities for artists and designers, including open calls, grants, fellowships, and residencies. Make sure you never miss out by joining our monthly&nbsp;<a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/newsletter/opportunities/">Opportunities Newsletter</a>.</p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.exhibizone.com/nuditas?SCH=75801" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Nuditas 2026: 5th Annual Juried Exhibition, Publication, Promotion, and Sales</a><span style="background-color: #ffdc13; padding: 2px 6px; margin-left: 8px; font-size: .9em; font-style: italic;"><strong>Featured</strong></span></strong><br>Ready to reveal the naked truth of the human body? From personal identity and body positivity to spirituality, mythology, emotion, and vulnerability, Nuditas 2026 celebrates the human form in all its expressions. Submit your strongest figurative or abstract works for the opportunity to exhibit internationally, be featured on Artsy, published in the official catalogue, and promoted worldwide.<br>Learn more and submit: <a href="https://www.exhibizone.com/nuditas?SCH=75801" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">www.exhibizone.com/nuditas</a><br><strong><em>Deadline: 11:59 p.m. PST on August 13, 2026</em></strong>.</p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.archenemyarts.com/opencall" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Arch Enemy Arts Call for Artists</a><span style="background-color: #ffdc13; padding: 2px 6px; margin-left: 8px; font-size: .9em; font-style: italic;"><strong>Featured</strong></span></strong><br>Arch Enemy Arts is seeking submissions for an annual group exhibition in January 2027. This spotlight exhibition of new and emerging talent has no themes or direction in subject matter, although the gallery focuses on representational, dark surrealism, magical realism, post-graffiti, pop-surrealism, narrative, illustrative, and figurative work across a range of artistic mediums. The exhibition is open to artists worldwide, who are invited to submit up to three works for consideration.<br><strong><em>Deadline: 11:59 p.m. EST on November 13, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p>&nbsp;</p>



<p><strong><strong style="font-size: 1.2em;">Open Calls</strong></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.thebritishartprize.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">The British Art Prize</a></strong> <em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>The British Art Prize, run by <em>Artists &amp; Illustrators</em> magazine, is one of the U.K.’s most exciting annual art competitions showcasing the talent and diversity of contemporary artists from around the world. Each year, a panel of leading curators, gallerists, and art professionals selects a shortlist of outstanding works. These finalists are exhibited at London’s Oxo Gallery. Winners are awarded prizes worth more than £10,000, including cash awards, art materials, a solo exhibition at Panter &amp; Hall’s Cecil Court Gallery, and editorial features in <em>Artists &amp; Illustrators</em>.<br><strong><em>Deadline: 5 p.m. BST on August 7, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.codaworx.com/rfq/detail/xx" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Clotilda Memorial Alabama Historical Commission</a></strong>&nbsp;<em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>The Alabama Historical Commission is seeking proposals to honor the last known African captives trafficked to the United States through the transatlantic slave trade: the <a href="https://theclotildamemorial.info/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Clotilda</a> survivors. The memorial will convey dimensions of the survivors’ lives and legacies—celebrating their resilient and determined spirits amidst violent dislocation, enslavement, and discrimination. Projects will be developed through a collaborative process that will engage the community founded by the Clotilda survivors and other formerly enslaved people: historic Africatown and the expansive diaspora. The total budget is $2,000,000.<br><strong><em>Deadline: 11:59 p.m. CDT on August 9, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><strong><a href="http://artistonish.com/calls?SCH=97101" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Publish Your Art in <em>Artistonish </em>Magazine and Sell on Artsy</a></strong></strong><em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>Submit works of art for the 73rd issue of <em>Artistonish</em> Contemporary Art Magazine, featuring juried contemporary works online and on premium glossy print pages. Each selected artwork receives a full-page image, dedicated QR code, Artsy feature for sales visibility, certificate of achievement, exclusive artwork badges, global promotion, and lasting online presence within the international art community. There is no fee to apply; selected artists pay a selection fee of $45.<br><strong><em>Deadline: 11:59 p.m. PDT on August 11, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.thewildcanvasretreat.art/sketch-contest" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">The Wild Canvas Sketch Challenge to Win a Puerto Rico Art Retreat</a></strong><em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>The Wild Canvas is organizing its inaugural art retreat in Ceiba, Puerto Rico, which invites up to 12 artists for a week-long program in January 2027. A sketching contest around the theme of &#8220;Island Time&#8221; provides a chance to win a fully funded spot, plus additional scholarships.<br><em style="font-weight: bold;"><strong>Deadline: August 25, 2026.</strong></em></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://spruillarts.org/amplify/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">AMPLIFY Mural Open Call</a></strong><em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(U.S.)</mark></em></em><br>The Spruill Gallery in Dunwoody, Georgia, is accepting nationwide submissions for its annual AMPLIFY mural competition. The winning artist will receive a $10,000 prize, and their mural will adorn the side of the historic Spruill Smoke House for the coming year.<br><em style="font-weight: bold;"><strong>Deadline: 11:59 p.m. EDT on August 28, 2026.</strong></em></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScrqxHab5NmFYGLgAXOWfejyt3jnPgcRBI6CeLusz1dzPu-YQ/viewform" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">ARTLittle 1st International Metaverse Art Expo</a> </strong><em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>The 1st International Metaverse Art Expo, presented by ARTLittle, is a 3D multiuser online exhibition where visitors from around the world walk through the galleries with avatars, discover artworks, and buy directly. ARTLittle is an independent art project built in Malaysia and is open to artists and galleries worldwide. Three hundred artists will be selected for exhibition in the virtual expo and have works offered for sale.<br><strong><em>Deadline: 11:59 p.m. MYT on August 31, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.huntmuseum.com/whats-on/hunt-museum-open-submission-exhibition-2026/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Hunt Museum Open Submission Exhibition</a></strong> <em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>The Hunt Open Submission Exhibition is an initiative celebrating contemporary Irish and international art at the Hunt Museum in Limerick. There is a €15 entry fee for the first image, plus an additional €15 per artwork for up to three submissions.<br><strong><em>Deadline: September 7, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.hidinginplainsite.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Hiding in Plain Site: <strong>International Public Art Short Film Festival</strong></a></strong> <em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>HPS invites filmmakers, artists, and creative practitioners to submit short works between two and 20 minutes for consideration in this screening program, which will premiere on October 25 in Minneapolis. HPS seeks to bring together film, video art, experimental media, XR (extended reality), and other works that expand how public art is experienced and represented. <br><strong><em>Deadline: September 10, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.mendocinoartcenter.org/teach" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Apply to Teach at Mendocino Art Center</a></strong> <em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(U.S.)</mark></em><br>The Mendocino Art Center (MAC), located in the coastal Northern California community of Mendocino, offers workshops taught by both visiting and local artists in a wide variety of mediums and topics. Some instructors choose to be compensated, and some choose to teach pro bono to help MAC offer more affordable workshops.<br><strong><em>Deadline: Rolling.</em></strong></p>



<p>&nbsp;</p>



<p><strong><strong style="font-size: 1.2em;">Grants</strong></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.bigfieldfund.org/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Big Fields Fund Grants for Eastern Iowa Artists</a></strong> <em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(Iowa)</mark></em><br>The Big Field Fund awards grants to artists and collectives to support publicly-engaged experimental, collaborative, and connective visual arts projects in eastern Iowa. Project grants award $8,000 to support the public realization of artist-led projects, while research and development grants offer $3,000 to support artists in the early stages of an ambitious project.<br><strong><em>Deadline: August 1, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://skogart.org/blog/5haqp3iqd3tkygl6iponogv3fyl8bx" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">SKOG Art Space Exhibitions Open Call</a></strong> <em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em><br>This open call welcomes artists from around the world at all career stages to apply for both solo and group exhibitions at SKOG in Oslo, Norway. The gallery welcomes proposals from both emerging and established artists working across all media and techniques.<br><strong><em>Deadline: August 16, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://artsmidwest.org/get-support/midwest-culture-bearers-award/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Midwest Culture Bearers Award</a></strong> <em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(Midwest)</mark></em><br>The Midwest Culture Bearers Award honors and amplifies the work of 18 mid-career and established Midwestern cultural practitioners each year. Selected individuals will each receive a $5,000 unrestricted award. No cost share or match is required to receive these funds. Additionally, Arts Midwest offers awardees virtual professional development and networking opportunities, plus the opportunity to have a story written about their work.<br><strong><em>Deadline: August 18, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.anchorlightraleigh.com/brightwork-grants" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">2027 Brightwork Fellowship &amp; Grants</a></strong> <em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(North Carolina)</mark></em><br>Anchorlight, based in Raleigh, offers one fellowship and two grants for 2027. The Professional Development Grant amounts to $2,000, and the Studio Project Grant awards $3,000. The fellowship is a year-long program geared toward an artist who is at a pivotal point in their career, providing a 500+ square-foot studio space at Anchorlight, an exhibition opportunity in its gallery, and an unrestricted financial award of $50,000. One artist will be selected for each, and each must have lived in North Carolina for at least 12 months as of applying. There is a $10 application fee for each opportunity.<br><strong><em>Deadline: August 28, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><a href="https://www.jracraft.org/chrysalis-award.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener"><strong>2026 Chrysalis Award for Emerging Ceramic Artists</strong></a> <em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(U.S.)</mark></em></em><br>The Chrysalis Award was created by the James Renwick Alliance for Craft to support and inspire emerging craft artists in the United States. Eligible applicants are in the early stages of their professional artistic careers—regardless of age—and have completed their training within the past five years. This year’s award will recognize an emerging artist working in ceramics, who will receive a $5,000 unrestricted award, a one-year JRACraft membership, and the opportunity to present their work at a JRACraft event.<br><strong><em>Deadline: August 23, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.lsmartfund.org/grants" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Liu Shiming Artist Grants</a></strong> <em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(U.S.)</mark></em></em><br>Designed to support the work of visual artists during the first decade of their careers, the Liu Shiming Artist Grants support the creation or completion of new projects that explore the interplay between traditional cultural or historical influences and contemporary artistic practice. Up to five artists will be selected to receive a $5,000 grant.<br><strong><em>Deadline: August 31, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.dezi.work/artprize" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Dezi Art Prize</a></strong> <em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>This global juried art grant is geared toward emerging and early-career visual artists. Two winners each receive a $1,000 unrestricted grant, plus a featured profile. Ten finalists are named and featured. Open worldwide, all visual media is welcome, with entries scored on merit by an independent jury. There is a $30 application fee.<br><strong><em>Deadline: September 10, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.printedmatter.org/workgrant" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Printed Matter Publisher Work Grant</a></strong> <em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>Now in its third year, Printed Matter&#8217;s Publisher Work Grant program offers funding to independent presses with a history of artists’ book publishing, acknowledging awardees’ accomplishments in past work and providing the capacity-building funds to enable future book projects and publisher sustainability. In 2026, three unrestricted grants of $10,000 will be awarded to three independent artists’ book publishers. Printed Matter will also extend a featured exhibitor presence at a forthcoming Printed Matter NY or LA Art Book Fair to selected presses.<br><strong><em>Deadline: October 4, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://arrivalgallery.myflodesk.com/arrival-grant" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">ARRIVAL Gallery Micro Grant</a></strong>&nbsp;<em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>The ARRIVAL Grant is designed to keep support simple and accessible. Artists submit one original artwork to the current round, and once the round reaches 1,000 valid submissions, one eligible artist receives a&nbsp;£100 grant&nbsp;and a new round begins.<br><em><strong>Deadline: Rolling.</strong></em></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.gottliebfoundation.org/emergency-grant" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">The Adolf and Esther Gottlieb Emergency Grant</a></strong>&nbsp;<em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>This program provides one-time financial assistance to qualified painters, printmakers, and sculptors whose needs resulted from an unforeseen catastrophic incident and who lack the resources to meet that situation. Awardees typically receive $5,000 and up to $15,000.<br><em><strong>Deadline: Rolling.</strong></em></p>



<p><a href="https://pkf.org/apply/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener"><strong>Pollock-Krasner Foundation Grant</strong></a><em>&nbsp;<em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>The foundation welcomes applications from painters, sculptors, and artists working on paper, including printmakers. Grants are intended for one year and range up to $50,000. The artist’s circumstances determine the size of the grant, and professional exhibition history will be considered.<br><em><strong>Deadline: Rolling.</strong></em></p>

<p><strong style="font-size: 1.2em;">Residencies, Fellowships, &amp; More</strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://bigci.org/awards/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">BigCi Environmental Awards 2026</a></strong> <em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>Australian and international artists working in visual art, installation, multimedia, performance, literature, music, photography, filmmaking, and curating are invited to submit entries for the BigCi Environmental Awards 2026. Two winning artists will each receive a free four-week residency at BigCi, where they will have the opportunity to explore the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Wollemi, Blue Mountains, and Gardens of Stone National Parks in Australia. The winners also receive an AUD$5,000 award. There is an AUD$40 application fee.<br><em style="font-weight: bold;"><strong>Deadline: August 2, 2026.</strong></em></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://tada-residency.ch/en/residence" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">TaDA Residency 2027</a></strong> <em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>Each year, six jury-selected candidates have the opportunity to work with textile companies in Eastern Switzerland, use a local studio in Arbon, and extend their individual networks over a period of three months. At the <em>TaDA Spinnerei</em> event, also attended by international speakers, artists can present their projects to an interested public and discuss with experts.<br><strong style="font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">Deadline: August 12, 2026.</strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.surfacedesign.org/air_form/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Surface Design Association Artist-in-Residence Program</a></strong> <em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>The residency program facilitated by the Surface Design Association (SDA) is designed to build skills, leverage relationships, and offer support to early, mid-career, and established fiber artists as they undertake studio projects that inspire artistic growth. The residency is virtual, and the selected participant is provided with a $2,000 studio stipend to support projects during their time. There is no application fee, but applicants must be members of SDA.<br><strong style="font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">Deadline: August 14, 2026.</strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.cprnyc.org/events/opencall-2027airprogram" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Center for Performance Research AiR</a></strong> <em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(New York City)</mark></em></em><br>CPR&#8217;s residency supports artists working in contemporary dance, performance, and time-based art. The organization values experimental approaches to content, form, and aesthetics and encourages risk-taking, interdisciplinarity, and the unexpected. The residency runs for one year (January to December 2027) and includes a $2,000 stipend, 20 free hours of rehearsal space, and more.<br><strong style="font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">Deadline: 5 p.m. EDT on August 24, 2026.</strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.beamarts.gr/international-artist-residency" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">bEam arts Residency</a></strong> <em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>bEam arts is an independent, artist-led residency program located in Thessaloniki, Greece, which welcomes visual artists and writers. The program supports a vibrant studio practice for up to four visual artists and two writers to stay for one or two months. During the residency, bEam arts hosts monthly activities and provides artists with opportunities to connect, engage with one another, and expand their professional networks.&nbsp;Each cycle ends with a group exhibition. The cost is €1,850 per month, including accommodation.<br><strong style="font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">Deadline: August 24, 2026.</strong></p>



<p><a href="https://www.barca13.pt/en/avistavulcao/agora/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener"><strong>AVISTAVULCÃO</strong> <strong>Residency</strong></a> <em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(Europe)</mark></em></em><br>Part of the Culture Moves Europe initiative, this open call is for applications for a one-month artist-in-residence program focused on research and creation, to take place in March 2027, intended for an artist or artistic duo. Located on the Azares island of Faial, near the Capelinhos Volcano, the residency offers an immersion in a territory shaped by the power of geology, its insular nature, and the constant interplay between nature and human presence. <br><strong style="font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">Deadline: August 31, 2026.</strong></p>



<p><a href="https://helpmannacademy.com.au/helpmann-fellowships/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener"><strong>Helpmann Fellowships</strong> </a><em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(South Australia)</mark></em></em><br>Three Helpmann Fellowships of up to AUD $7,500 are available to support ambitious, self-directed projects that advance the artistic and professional development of recent graduates (within five years) of eligible performing and visual arts programs at South Australia&#8217;s two universities. Funding can support larger-scale creative projects, tailored professional development, or a combination of both.<br><strong style="font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">Deadline: 11:59 p.m. ACST on August 31, 2026.</strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.listasafn.is/en/art/news-vasulka-stofa/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">2027 National Gallery of Iceland Residency</a></strong><em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color"><em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em></mark></em></em><br>The National Gallery of Iceland is seeking applications to its CUSP program, a European cooperation project funded through Creative Europe’s Culture grant. Artists working in complex media or emerging technologies are invited to apply. The residency will be up to four weeks long, and accommodation, workspace, and stipends are provided.<br><strong style="font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">Deadline: 11:59 p.m. GMT on September 2, 2026.</strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://artssoutheast.org/onview-residency-app" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">ON::View Artist Residency Program</a></strong><em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>Located in the heart of Savannah’s Starland District at ARTS Southeast, the fully-funded ON::View Artist Residency provides a free, high-visibility studio space, lodging, and a $500 stipend for an artist or curator to complete a new project, continue an in-progress endeavor, or to conduct research. There is a $50 application fee.<br><strong><em>Deadline: 11:59 p.m. ET on September 7, 2026.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://www.macdowell.org/apply/apply-for-fellowship" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">MacDowell Fellowships for Spring/Summer 2027</a></strong><em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>Located in Peterborough, New Hampshire, MacDowell encourages applications from artists of all backgrounds and all countries in the following disciplines: architecture, film/video, interdisciplinary arts, literature, music composition, theatre, and visual arts. A Fellowship consists of exclusive use of a private studio, accommodations, and three prepared meals a day for two to eight weeks.<br><strong style="font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">Deadline: September 10, 2026.</strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://queensmuseum.org/program/open-call-2027-28-qm-jerome-foundation-fellowship-for-emerging-artists/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">2027-28 QM-Jerome Foundation Fellowship for Emerging Artists</a></strong><em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(New York City)</mark></em></em><br>The Queens Museum (QM) launches its eighth iteration of the QM-Jerome Foundation Fellowship for Emerging Artists in New York City. Two visual artists will receive $20,000 each and professional development consultations from QM staff members working toward an artist’s project. Each fellow will also receive mentorship from a New York-based established artist. The fellowships will culminate in solo project exhibitions at the Queens Museum in 2028. The duration of each fellowship is one year, culminating with the opening of the fellow’s exhibition.<br><strong style="font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">Deadline: 11:59 p.m. EDT on September 28, 2026.</strong></p>



<p><a href="https://quarantinemenorca.events/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener"><strong>Quarantine</strong></a> <em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>Dubbed &#8220;purgatory for artists,&#8221; Quarantine is a week-long intensive art program on an 18th-century quarantine island off the coast of Menorca, Spain. The program is open to beginners and professionals alike and offers three 45-minute private mentorships throughout the week, with activities lasting 12+ hours per day. Phones are banned.<br><strong><em>Deadline: Rolling.</em></strong></p>



<p><strong><a href="https://residenciacorazon.com.ar/artist-residency-program-argentina-residencia-corazon/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Residencia Corazón</a></strong> <em><em><mark style="background-color:rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" class="has-inline-color has-driftwood-color">(International)</mark></em></em><br>Residencia Corazón is an independent, artist-run residency in La<br>Plata, Argentina—a home for artists since 2006. The program welcomes visual<br>artists, writers, curators, and creative researchers from around the<br>world for one- to three-month residencies. Each stay is fully personalized, and fees range from $800 to $1,500 per month.<br><strong><em>Deadline: Rolling.</em></strong></p>

		<title>Innovation Meets Heritage in West African Contemporary Artists&#8217; Masquerade Ensembles</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/new-african-masquerades-exhibition-west-africa-masks-costumes-traditions/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Kate Mothes]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Wed, 29 Jul 2026 15:47:30 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[History]]></category>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-8.jpeg" alt="Innovation Meets Heritage in West African Contemporary Artists&#8217; Masquerade Ensembles" />'New African Masquerades: Artistic Innovations and Collaborations' celebrates contemporary creations by artists in Nigeria, Burkina Faso, Sierra Leone, and Cameroon.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/07/new-african-masquerades-exhibition-west-africa-masks-costumes-traditions/">Innovation Meets Heritage in West African Contemporary Artists&#8217; Masquerade Ensembles</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-8.jpeg" alt="Innovation Meets Heritage in West African Contemporary Artists&#8217; Masquerade Ensembles" />


<p>Across West Africa, Indigenous communities mark holidays, rites, and sacred events with a remarkable variety of ceremonies ranging from dances to processions. These <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masquerade_ceremony" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">masquerade traditions</a> incorporate meticulously carved masks and full-body costumes that often facilitate links between humans and the spiritual world. There&#8217;s evidence of masked customs dating back millennia, and today, artists continue the tradition of hand-hewn masks and ensembles in vivid colors and a wide array of materials—sometimes with a twist.</p>



<p>The exhibition <em>New African Masquerades: Artistic Innovations and Collaborations</em>, which opens at the <a href="https://mfastpete.org/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Museum of Fine Arts St. Petersburg</a> next month, celebrates contemporary creations by four artists: Chief Ekpenyong Bassey Nsa (Nigeria), David Sanou (Burkina Faso), Sheku “Goldenfinger” Fofanah (Sierra Leone), and Hervé Youmbi (Cameroon). Along with displays of some of their masks and full ensembles, visitors will be able to explore documentary photographs and videos of ceremonies and parades in addition to immersive multimedia experiences.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2667" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-5.jpeg" alt="a geometric mask and colorful raffia costume of an African masquerade ensemble" class="wp-image-476254" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-5.jpeg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-5-640x853.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-5-960x1280.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-5-768x1024.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-5-1152x1536.jpeg 1152w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-5-1536x2048.jpeg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Headpiece by André Sanou and body by anonymous artist, &#8220;Kimi&#8221; masquerade ensemble in honor of André Sanou&#8217;s &#8216;Qui Dit Miuex?&#8217; (2022). Collection of Fitchburg Art Museum, photo courtesy of the New Orleans Museum of Art</figcaption></figure>



<p>&#8220;Across many West African cultures, masquerade a broad range of artistic, social, spiritual, and civic traditions,&#8221; the museum says. &#8220;Encompassing sculpture, textiles, performance, music, movement, and community participation, these performance traditions continuously adapt to contemporary life.&#8221; Sanou&#8217;s geometric masks are bold and brightly painted, often paired with costumes made from colorfully dyed fiber. And one can even spot pop culture references in Youmbi&#8217;s &#8220;Tso Scream Mask,&#8221; for example, which coats the iconic visage from the <em>Scream </em>movie franchise with thousands of beads.</p>



<p><em>New African Masquerades </em>is conceived as a dynamic exploration of the masquerade tradition&#8217;s collaborative and community-based practices, inviting viewers to a kind of reverie where time-honored heritage meets constant innovation. The show is organized by the New Orleans Museum of Art in partnership with the Museé des Civilisations noires in Dakar, Senegal. The exhibition opens on August 15 and continues through January 3, 2027, in St. Pete, Florida. Follow updates on the museum&#8217;s <a href="https://www.instagram.com/mfastpete/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="3333" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-2.jpeg" alt="an elaborate and colorful African masquerade ensemble with beaded details and a face resembling the mask from 'Scream'" class="wp-image-476249" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-2.jpeg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-2-640x1067.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-2-960x1600.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-2-768x1280.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-2-922x1536.jpeg 922w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-2-1229x2048.jpeg 1229w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Hervé Youmbi (Cameroon), &#8220;Tso Scream Mask&#8221; from the &#8216;Visage de masques (IX) series&#8217; (2015-2023), wood, pigment, fiber, beads, textile, glue, velvet fabric, cotton fabric, silk embroidery, and horse hair. Collection of the New Orleans Museum of Art</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1631" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-4.jpg" alt="an African masquerade ceremonial procession consisting of four figures in elaborate head-to-toe costumes" class="wp-image-476253" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-4.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-4-640x522.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-4-960x783.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-4-768x626.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-4-1536x1253.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Hervé Youmbi, &#8220;Tso Scream Mask&#8221; and &#8220;Tso Scream Leopard Mask&#8221; at the Nka&#8217;a Kossié society succession ceremony at Fondanti Chieftancy (December 3, 2022). Photo by Hervé Youmbi, courtesy of the artist and Axis Gallery, New York and New Jersey</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2512" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-7.jpeg" alt="an elaborate and colorful African masquerade ensemble" class="wp-image-476250" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-7.jpeg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-7-640x804.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-7-960x1206.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-7-768x965.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-7-1223x1536.jpeg 1223w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-7-1631x2048.jpeg 1631w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Sheku &#8220;Goldenfinger&#8221; Fofanah (Sierra Leone), &#8220;Fairy Masquerade Ensemble&#8221; (2022), fabric, sequins, wood, paint, and glue, life-size. Commission for the Fitchburg Art Museum, photo courtesy of the New Orleans Museum of Art</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1333" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-3.jpg" alt="Three figures dance in masks with long black braid-like ropes during a ceremony" class="wp-image-476252" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-3.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-3-640x427.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-3-960x640.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-3-768x512.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-3-1536x1024.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Hervé Youmbi, &#8220;Bamiléké-Kwele Ku&#8217;ngang Gorilla Mask&#8221; and &#8220;Single-faced Rhino Mask&#8221; during a ceremony in Fondanti village (2019). Photo by Hervé Youmbi, courtesy of the artist and Axis Gallery, New York and New Jersey</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1333" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-6.jpeg" alt="a photograph of geometric &quot;Kimi&quot; masks and colorful raffia costumes during a ceremonial performance" class="wp-image-476255" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-6.jpeg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-6-640x427.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-6-960x640.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-6-768x512.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-6-1536x1024.jpeg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Headpieces by David Sanou, studio of André Sanou, &#8220;Kimi&#8221; masks during a performance of greetings with the lead griot Tchiedo playing his drum behind them (May 3, 2022),  Bindougosso district, Bobo-Dioulasso, Burkina Faso. Photo by Lisa Homann</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2589" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-9.jpeg" alt="an elaborate African masquerade costume with white raffia ruffles and large armlets and anklets" class="wp-image-476257" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-9.jpeg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-9-640x828.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-9-960x1243.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-9-768x994.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-9-1187x1536.jpeg 1187w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-9-1582x2048.jpeg 1582w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Chief Ekpenyong Bassey Nsa (Nigeria), &#8220;Afia Awan Masquerade Ensemble&#8221; (2022), polyester fabric, raffia, and leather, life-size. Collection of the New Orleans Museum of Art</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1796" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-1.jpg" alt="an elaborate and colorful African masquerade ensemble parades down the street amid a group of people" class="wp-image-476248" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-1.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-1-640x575.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-1-960x862.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-1-768x690.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/masquerade-1-1536x1379.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Sheky &#8220;Goldenfinger&#8221; Fofanah parading with his Mami Wata devil during the Massaboni Ordehlay procession (December 26, 2022), Lunsar, Sierra Leone. Photo by Amanda M. Maples</figcaption></figure>
